About this document


This document provides the teaching content for Textiles Technology Years 11–13 of
the New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Textiles Technology Years 11–13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Textiles Technology Years 11–13 is proposed
to be made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under
section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Textiles Technology Years 11–13 will be required to start using it in Year 11
from 1 January 2028, in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January
2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

  Students are taught about the performance properties of natural and man-made                  industry pathways.
  fibres and textiles, anthropometrics, ethical responsibility, and identifying
  sustainable practices for textiles. They are taught how to apply processes and
  techniques such as using creative problem-solving and textile design thinking,
  material development and innovation, pattern use and making, textile
  construction techniques, applied aesthetic and functional finishings, to produce
  fit-for-purpose products.


Through the study of Textiles Technology students are taught to apply textile
materials and processes using an iterative user-centred design framework to develop
sustainable and fit-for-purpose outcomes. They examine how anthropometric and
dimensional data, material properties, stakeholder requirements, and ethical and
environmental considerations inform the design, development, evaluation, and
refinement of textile products.
Textiles Technology provides students with the knowledge and practices to explore
the relationship between the human body, textile materials, and product performance.
This disciplinary knowledge enables students to develop an understanding of how to
manage uncertainty through ongoing cycles of noticing, defining, ideating, analysing,
developing, creating, and evaluating outcomes.
As students progress through Years 11–13, they learn to justify design decisions
using evidence, balancing performance, durability, cost, and sustainability, while
creating innovative textile solutions that respond to user needs and industry contexts.
Students integrate scientific understanding, design thinking, and ethical decision-
making to evaluate the impacts of design choices and address social, cultural,
environmental, and technological challenges.

 Disciplinary Writing

 Focus: the use of writing to reflect the ways in which knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within Textiles Technology.

 In Textiles Technology, writing is an analytical and reflective practice enabling students to develop and refine ideas and communicate informed understandings of their own and others’ work.
